title: Code for each step: a project's pipeline as code that recomputes its holdout number in a clean environment
request: Each step renders its code (a notebook cell and a module) from the records, readable by a data scientist; the whole pipeline as a notebook and a package; done when for every family supported in the engine the exported pipeline runs in a clean environment and reproduces its holdout number.
spec: A folder per project: pipeline.py with one block per step, the same cells as a notebook, the data it reads, dclab_core, pinned requirements and the recorded number; a route giving it as a zip; a check that runs every engine kind's export in a fresh Python 3.12.
plan: Survey what the notebook and service exports already do and whether anything reruns exported code.
Write each own-machine kind as dclab_core calls mirroring its machine; write tabular projects as the engine's runner on the prepared rows.
Run every kind's export, then build the clean-environment check.

decisions.decision: A kind with its own machine is written as dclab_core calls from the raw tables.
decisions.why: Its library already holds every step; calling it with the recorded choices is both readable and exact.

decisions.decision: A tabular project ships the rows as the engine prepared them and the engine's runner.
decisions.why: Its preparation lives in the studio; the recipe, the model and the score can be reproduced exactly, and the preparation is said rather than imitated.

decisions.decision: The clean check uses one fresh Python 3.12 with only the pinned requirements every export names.
decisions.why: No repository, no dclab_rnd and no development environment can help the code reproduce its number.

decisions.decision: Exporting the code is a write action written to the audit trail.
decisions.why: The folder holds the person's data.

change: dclab_rnd/studio/code.py (new), scripts/code_check.py (new), Makefile (code-check), agentic/routers/projects.py (the zip route), accounts/guard.py (write permission), audit.py (data_export), the web client; tests/test_code.py (new); the plan, the roadmap, CLAUDE.md.

findings.defect: Ignoring the engine's model sizes went unnoticed.
findings.scenario: A planted fault dropped the recorded profile and every test passed.
findings.cause: The tested replicas chose models the profile does not change.
findings.fix: A test checks the recorded profile is carried into the code; the clean check covers the families it changes.

findings.defect: An own-machine kind always read its tables as CSV.
findings.scenario: A project built from Home keeps its table as parquet: the exported code crashed on its first read.
findings.cause: The templates called the CSV reader; related tables were saved again as CSV, changing their types.
findings.fix: The code reads each table by its file's format, copied byte for byte; the reader's package joins the requirements.

findings.defect: A person's choice over the rule's made the exported code fail.
findings.scenario: Approving another detector before the final stage made the code's check of the choice fail.
findings.cause: The code checked the rule's pick made again against the person's choice.
findings.fix: The rule's pick is checked against the rule's, the person's choice scored, and the code says so.

findings.defect: With a time-and-group split the exported code trained on rows of the holdout period.
findings.scenario: Later rows of a household seen in training, in neither part, were trained on: the number moved from 0.75017 to 0.75250.
findings.cause: Only the holdout was marked; every other row was taken as training.
findings.fix: Each row is marked train, holdout or neither.

findings.scenario: Features scaled by 1e-11 were rounded to zero by the ten-digit text format and the number moved.
findings.cause: JSON text with ten decimal places.
findings.fix: The rows are kept as a pandas pickle written by the pinned pandas.

findings.defect: A project name outside Latin-1 made the download fail.
findings.scenario: A Persian project name raised an encoding error in the response header after the zip was built.
findings.cause: The name went into the header as is.
findings.fix: An ASCII file name, and the real one encoded for browsers that read it.

findings.defect: A reader could download every table of a project with no audit row.
findings.scenario: A viewer's read permission was enough for the code route, which carries the raw tables or the prepared rows with labels.
findings.cause: A GET route needs only read by default.
findings.fix: The route needs the write permission, and each export writes a data_export row with the files' hashes.

findings.defect: Changed data made the route fail with a server error.
findings.scenario: A table whose fingerprint no longer matched raised past the route.
findings.fix: Data errors answer 409 with their reason.

findings.defect: The clean check could cover fewer kinds, or skip, without saying so.
findings.scenario: A kind without a replica would be dropped silently; any message with 'not found' counted as a missing Python.
findings.cause: A filter and a loose match.
findings.fix: Kinds without a replica fail the check by name; only uv's own message is a skip.

findings.defect: Some steps had no block, and the forecast's choice was never checked.
findings.scenario: Tabular code had no leakage block; the forecast computed its validation and discarded it.
findings.cause: Blocks written only where a call was needed.
findings.fix: A leakage block for tabular projects, feature blocks for the own-machine kinds, and the forecast's rule applied again and checked.

measurements.name: every kind the engine runs, in a clean Python 3.12
measurements.gate: each kind's exported code reproduces its recorded holdout number within 1e-6, in a fresh environment holding only the pinned requirements
measurements.result: 12 of 12 reproduced: binary, multiclass, regression, rare_event, text_tabular, places, entity_tables, forecasting, time_to_event, streams, anomaly, embedded, in Python 3.12.13
limits: A tabular project's preparation is shipped as its result, not re-run.

measurements.name: planted faults
measurements.gate: each planted fault fails a test
measurements.result: 10 of 12 planted faults caught; the 2 left: the profile on replicas whose models ignore it (now checked by a test), and the positive class, which the refitted ROC-AUC cannot see

outcome: A project's pipeline exports as readable code, one block per step, that recomputes its holdout number; every kind the engine runs does so exactly in a clean Python 3.12.
lessons: Read a table the way the product read it: a format assumed is a crash on the first real project.
A split has three parts when groups and time meet: mark the rows in neither, or they drift into training.
Text formats round numbers; keep data losslessly when a number must come back exactly.
risks: A tabular project's preparation is not re-run as code.
The main product's code snapshots are not filled.
Images have no code until they run in the engine.
